note: Real-data questions for tools/county_check.py (stage 3). Written by the planning chat; no session edits this file, and no question here may be used as an example in a prompt. 'thread' seeds earlier ANSWERED turns with the counts they ran. 'expect': 'status' lists the statuses that pass; 'counts' is the exact set of counts that must have run after filling, each as source, period, filters and group_by in the tool's own shape (null = not checked; filters compared as a set, age ends that are missing mean the usable limit); 'compare' and 'share' say whether one was made (null = not checked); 'kind' is the reply kind or null. Numbers are not checked here: Python makes them, and the chat checks Python against its own counts. C17 assumes the copy's last finished month is October 2026. Version 2 (2026-11-13) adds S01 to S12, statistics: 'analyses' is the exact list of analyses that must have run (kind, source, filters and options, compared after the program's own tidying; the period is not compared, and 'window', where given, is the first and last month used; null or absent = not checked; [] = none may run). A thread turn with 'trend' is replayed by running that trend, which needs R. S01's window assumes the copy's last finished month is October 2026 and one month dropped. Version 3 (13 Nov, planning chat on Opus 5.5): `expect_or` lists other right answers, read from the live run of 13 November: C06 one count of both years by year (its groups say which is higher); C12 the two-year range 16 to 17 with C28's line; S12 the two groups the other way round. S05: the same with year held fixed. Version 4 (14 Nov, planning chat on Opus 5.5): T01 to T03, a question about the data itself, from Nino's Slack thread of 14 November (a thread turn with 'talk' is replayed as that talk reply); G01 to G03, plain messages that hold a word of stage 1's rule 1 list (forget, confirm that, say that), which must reach the model. Version 5 (14 Nov, planning chat on Opus 5.5, Nino: 'can you ask more natural questions?'): N01 to N15, questions as people type them in Slack (lower case, no question mark, 'ppl', 'last year', 'make that a chart'); where more than one right way exists, only the status and kind are checked. Version 6 (14 Nov afternoon, planning chat on Opus 5.5, D-066 'keep looking for bugs ... better natural language'): N16 to N45, a sweep of plain questions across the other sources, typos, follow-ups, two questions at once, loose statistics and rates, what he cannot do, and small talk. Version 7 (14 Nov, planning chat on Opus 5.5): C24 also passes with NEEDS_INPUT, a question back about which records to compare (live round 14: the right reply to 'more dangerous' is to say what the records can and cannot show and ask which to compare). Version 8 (16 Nov, planning chat on Fable 5.2; the Fable review's PROOF GAP 1: 26 cases passed on their status alone, so a wrong count passed): 24 of them now name the counts or analyses that must have run, read from Haiku test 2 of 16 November where every reply was read and right, with `expect_or` for the other right ways (two counts or one count by year; a short repeat as talk; a question back for N24 and N37; N34's two directions, each also with year held fixed). Two stay on status alone and every run of them is read by hand: C24 (several right replies) and N07 (the busiest day of the week: the right answer is a count by weekday or the day named from the timing analysis; the timing reply names the busiest hour, which does not answer it). Version 9 (17 Nov, planning chat on Fable 5.2; CHAT-BUILDS-check-6, step 7, doubts 1 to 4): G03 no longer passes as talk (a talk text cannot hold the figure); N28 also passes with one count of the two districts broken down by district; N30 also with 2024 alone and 2025 by district; N31 also with 1 August 2024. Left as they are and read by hand: a question back passes N24 and N37 whatever it asks (doubt 5); the same days written another way fail a count case, N04 above all (doubt 6).
